video.title: If You Don't Understand Debt, You Don't Understand Business

summary: Codie Sanchez explains how wealthy people use debt: borrowing against securities instead of selling, buying businesses with SBA loans and seller financing, mortgages, and credit cards for float. She walks through a Texas lawn care business ($349k ask, $144k cash flow) bought with 10% down for a claimed 265% cash-on-cash return, and a seller-financed version paying 40% of profits. She warns about personal guarantees, margin calls, overpriced listings like a boat rental, and credit card balances. The video promotes her Contrarian community, Boardroom programme and a SoFi sponsorship.

tactics.name: Borrow against assets instead of selling
steps: Take a securities-backed line of credit against a portfolio
Keep LTV at 20-30% for stocks, under 10% for crypto
Pay interest from salary/business cash flow; ask CPA about deductibility
Avoid margin calls by not over-borrowing

tactics.name: Structure a seller-financed acquisition
steps: Put ~10% down
Offer seller a higher total (e.g. $375k vs $349k ask) paid over 7 years
Pay seller a fixed share (40%) of profits until repaid
Skip the bank

quote.text: you give the seller 40% of the profits until you pay back the 375 over these seven years
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

tactics.name: Screen listings on cash flow vs price
steps: Compare asking price to cash flow
Check seasonality and hidden costs (e.g. captain)
Renegotiate or walk away

tactics.name: Augusta rule (US)
steps: Rent your home to your business up to 14 days a year for meetings
Document properly; check with CPA

tactics.name: Use business credit cards for float and rewards
steps: Pay in full monthly
Use 0% intro and cashback cards
Issue virtual cards with limits to staff (Ramp-style)
Pay off existing debt via snowball or avalanche

tactics.name: Prioritise before extra mortgage payments
steps: Max retirement accounts
Kill debt above 10% interest
Build cash buffer
Then consider extra principal

warnings.warning: SBA loans carry personal guarantees; failure lets the SBA pursue your house and assets.

quote.text: If you buy a business with an SBA loan and it goes out of business before the loan is repaid, the SBA will come after everything
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: Over-borrowing against assets causes margin calls and forced sales at the worst time.

quote.text: Robinhood lets you do one-to-one leverage
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

warnings.warning: Carrying a credit card balance at ~22% turns float into disaster.
Overpriced seasonal businesses (e.g. boat rental) can have negligible profit.
Buying a business you don't know how to run, without due diligence, is the main way acquisitions fail.

lessons.lesson: Borrow to buy cash-producing, appreciating assets, not to consume.

quote.text: Some people use debt to buy things that make them look rich. Other people use debt to buy things that make them free
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: Leveraged acquisition of a cash-flowing business can far outperform index investing.
Seller financing is common and lets you buy with less cash.
Retiring boomers create a wave of businesses for sale.
Increasing profit raises business value by the sale multiple.
A house is often a lifestyle purchase, not automatically an investment; compare total cost of owning.
Never risk what you have and need for what you don't have and don't need.

quote.text: Never risk what you have in need for what you do not have and do not need
quote.speaker: Codie Sanchez

lessons.lesson: The goal is a business that runs without you.

quote.text: The goal was never a business you run. It's a business that runs without you
